findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?` so it never gates serialization
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always included in the payload, even when the website is blank (serialized as `null`). Rename to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 website to anonymous users
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user seen by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, so the website host (and now possibly the full path) is still exposed for TL0 users to anonymous visitors, defeating the existing spam-prevention restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and extend the TL0 spec's `untrusted_attributes` list accordingly.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and parses the URI repeatedly
findings.body: `website_host` and `Discourse.current_hostname` are compared with `==`/`ends_with?` without downcasing. A profile URL such as `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` yields host `EXAMPLE.com` which will not match hostname `example.com`, so the full-path behaviour this PR adds silently fails. Downcase both hosts before comparing. (`URI(website.to_s)` is also built three times; parse once.)

findings.title: Subdomain match only works when label counts are equal
findings.body: The second branch requires `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and >2 labels, so cases like website `www.example.com` with instance `forum.eu.example.com`, or website `example.co.uk` with instance `forum.example.co.uk` (handled only by the `ends_with?` branch, which works) are inconsistent: sibling subdomains with different depths fall back to host-only. Consider comparing registrable suffixes instead of label counts.

findings.title: Use `+` instead of `<<` for string concatenation here
findings.body: `"." << website_host` mutates the receiver string in place; while the literal is a fresh object today, this breaks if `# frozen_string_literal: true` is ever added to the file and is needlessly surprising. Use `"." + website_host`.

findings.title: No test for sibling-subdomain and blank-website cases
findings.body: The new specs cover only equal host, different host, and parent-domain host. Missing: website blank/invalid (verifying `website_name` is omitted, which currently fails because `include_website_name?` is misnamed), and the sibling subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance) which is the most fragile piece of the new logic.
